newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian leaders declare war against corruption.
newsitem.headline: Indian leaders declare war against corruption.

text.p: India's leaders called for a war against corruption on Friday as the nation took a sobering look at 50 years of freedom from colonial rule.

President K.R. Narayanan and Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral appealed to citizens in nationally televised speeches to launch a mass movement in the tradition of Mahatma Gandhi to stamp out pervasive graft.

Their emphasis on bribery came at a time of a string criminal cases against senior politicians and candid introspection on the 50th anniversary of independence, which was ushered in on Thursday evening with a dazzling show of laser beams and parades.

"I am painfully aware of the deterioration that has taken place in our country and in our society in recent times," Narayanan told a meeting of parliament that convened at the stroke of midnight and recalled India's "tryst with destiny".

"Sheer opportunism and value-less power-politics have taken over the place of principles and idealism that had been the hallmark of our social and political life...corruption is corroding the vitals of our politics and our society.
"A social movement or a widespread national movement is needed to cleanse the system," India's first low-caste president told parliamentarians and foreign dignitaries.
Gujral, speaking in the early morning from the sandstone ramparts of the 17th century Red Fort in the capital, said corruption was corroding the vitals of politics and society.

"Our war against corruption is honest and candid," he said. "And for this, we have to build a mass movement, in which all can join so that corruption in politics, politicians and public life must end."
Gujral, who devoted much of his 75-minute speech to the ills of graft, said Indians must start a non-cooperation movement along the lines of Mahatma Gandhi's "Satyagraha", or civil disobedience.
"Let us all resolve today that we would not give a single penny as a bribe to get our work done at any level," he said.
Laloo Prasad Yadav, the former leader of Gujral's Janata Dal party, has been indicted in a $280 million scandal in Bihar state. He says he is innocent.
Former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao of the Congress party has been indicted in two criminal corruption cases. He denies any wrongdoing.

On Thursday evening at the start of the anniversary celebrations, thousands of people led by old and frail "freedom fighters" marched with the Indian tricolour flag down a wide avenue flanked by twinkling lights.

Singers and dancers staged a joyous celebration on a giant stage at Vijay Chowk (Victory Square) a stone's throw from Parliament House where hundreds of lawmakers gathered in the majestic Central Hall to recreate their nation's "tryst with destiny" at the stroke of midnight on August 14-15, 1947.

"Long years ago we made a tryst with destiny... At the stroke of the midnight hour, when the world sleeps, India will awake to life and freedom," the new nation's first prime minister Jawaharlal Nehru said in a 1947 speech replayed in Parliament House during the midnight ceremony.
